transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I came in today because... my mind just will not hold onto things anymore. It's getting really frustrating. 

I'll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program I help out with—something I could do in my sleep before, really. But now, I just sit there and the numbers and words just kind of scatter on me. I just can't seem to think straight or focus like I used to.
When did you first start noticing these problems with your memory and concentration, and how long has this been going on?
It's been about three weeks now. I'd say that's when I first started noticing it. It all just... well, it started right after my older sister passed away.
Since your sister passed away, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or empty most of the day?

Yes, I have. Most days, I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling right in my chest. It just kind of stays with me all day. Even when my wife is right there, talking kindly to me... I just feel like I'm sitting at the bottom of a well. It's a very empty feeling.
Besides the sadness, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like your work with the youth program or other hobbies?

Yes, I have. I just... I haven't even touched the wood pieces I had laid out on my bench. I usually enjoy that, but now they're just sitting there. I've also skipped out on planning for the choir, and I haven't been to chess either. Even fishing... it just sounds like more effort than it's worth right now. That's really not like me at all.
Have you been experiencing feelings of worthlessness, or excessive guilt about things—perhaps even guilt related to your sister's death—that feel out of proportion to the situation?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I miss my sister terribly, of course, but... I don't feel guilty about her passing. It was just her time, I suppose. And as for feeling worthless... no, I don't think so. I just feel incredibly sad and tired all the time. But I don't feel like I'm a bad person or anything like that.
Since your sister passed away, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, such as trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

No, my sleep hasn't really changed. I mean, I go to bed around the same time I always do, and I usually sleep through the night. I'm definitely tired during the day, like I mentioned, but I don't think I'm sleeping more than normal or having trouble getting to sleep. It's just... the regular amount, I guess.
Have you had any thoughts about death or dying, or thoughts of not wanting to be alive?

Yes, I have. I just keep thinking that... well, that my family might actually be better off without me around. And to be honest, when I'm out near my workshop, I... I get scared of where my thoughts could go if I were left alone out there.
Besides the sadness, have you been feeling especially nervous, tense, or on edge since your sister's death?
No, not really. I haven't felt nervous or tense. It's... it's mostly just the sadness, like I said. I don't feel on edge at all, really. Just very heavy and tired, I suppose.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a persistent (3-week) depressive syndrome that emerged after a significant loss (sister's death), including depressed mood most of the day, marked anhedonia (withdrawal from woodworking, choir, chess, fishing), cognitive impairment (poor concentration/memory), fatigue, and passive suicidal ideation with some concerning ideation near his workshop. These symptoms exceed the expected intensity and functional impact of normal bereavement, meeting criteria for a major depressive episode. Absence of guilt/worthlessness and sleep disturbance does not preclude the diagnosis given the required symptom count is otherwise met. Anxiety symptoms were explicitly denied, making a primary anxiety disorder unlikely. Because this appears to be a single episode without stated prior history, and severity/psychotic features are not specified, F32.9 (Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified) is the most accurate code. Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.21) was considered given the clear precipitating stressor, but the full depressive syndrome (5+ core symptoms, functional impairment, suicidal ideation) surpasses the adjustment disorder threshold.
